title: Elevator system design
idea: An elevator design keeps pending stops per direction, serves them in one sweep before turning, and lets a dispatcher pick which car answers a call.

analogy.text: A delivery van heading north drops every parcel on its northbound streets first, then turns round and serves the southbound ones.
analogy.breaks: Van routes are planned ahead; elevator stops arrive while it moves.

points: A request above the car joins `upStops`; a request below joins `downStops`.
Both sets are sorted `TreeSet`s, so the next stop is first or last.
The car keeps its direction while stops remain ahead, then turns.
A `DispatchStrategy` picks which car takes a hall call; swap it to change policy.

hero.title: One car, two sorted stop sets

steps.caption: The car rests at floor 0. Both stop sets are empty.
Calls for 5 and 2 are above the car, so both join `upStops`, kept sorted.
`step` takes the lowest up stop. The car moves up to floor 2.
A call for 1 arrives. It is below the car, so it waits in `downStops`.
A call for 8 is above the car, so it joins the current upward sweep.
Stops remain ahead, so the car keeps going up to 5.
Then 8. Now no stops remain above the car.
Only now does it turn and serve floor 1 going down.

code.title: One car sweeps
code.caption: The scenario from the animation. Each `step` prints where the car stops and its direction.

walk.text: An `enum` names the only three directions a car can have.
Two sorted sets of pending stops, plus the car's floor and direction.
A request lands in the set on its side of the car's current floor.
Keep the current direction while it has stops; otherwise turn.
`pollFirst` gives the nearest stop above; `pollLast` the nearest below.
Calls for 1 and 8 arrive after the car has left floor 0.

code.title: Pick a car
code.caption: Three cars, three hall calls. The strategy prefers the nearest car already heading that way.

walk.text: A car is approaching if it is idle or the call lies ahead of it.
The dispatch contract: given the cars and a floor, return one car.
Pick the car with the lowest cost.
A car moving away gets a large penalty instead of being excluded.
`main` sends three calls through the same strategy.

pitfalls: Do not serve calls in arrival order; the car zigzags and riders wait longer.
Guard `request` and `step` with one lock when buttons and the motor run concurrently.
Model doors and motion as `enum` states so a moving car never opens doors.

quiz.q: What does `DispatchDemo` print for the call at floor 1?
quiz.why: A climbs away from floor 1, so it pays the penalty. B descends from 6 toward 1, cost 5, beating idle C at cost 8.

takeaway: Sort stops per direction, sweep before turning, and dispatch through a strategy.

starters: How would I add a State pattern for doors open, moving and maintenance?
What changes when the building has eight cars instead of three?
How do I make the elevator thread-safe with real button presses?
